title.sl: Oziralni stavki: who, which, that, where, whose
title.de: Relativsätze: who, which, that, where, whose
title.it: Le relative: who, which, that, where, whose
title.en: Relative clauses: who, which, that, where, whose

rule.sl:
**Oziralni stavek** pove, katero osebo ali stvar misliš. Stoji za samostalnikom, brez vejice, čeprav jo slovenščina zahteva.

**who** je za ljudi: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** (Mož, ki živi zraven, je kovač.) **which** je za stvari: **the bus which goes to Keswick**. **that** je za oboje in je zelo pogost: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down**.

Če takoj za besedo pride nov osebek, je beseda predmet in lahko odpade: **the cheese (that) Arthur likes** (sir, ki ga ima Arthur rad), **the man (who) I met**. Kot osebek ostane: **the man who lives next door**. Dodatnega zaimka ni: **the book I read** (knjiga, ki sem jo prebral), nikoli *the book I read it*.

**where** je za kraje: **the inn where we had lunch**. **whose** stoji za his, her, their: **the man whose dog won** (mož, čigar pes je zmagal). Mali predlog ostane na koncu: **the woman I spoke to**, **the inn we had lunch at**.

Ljudje rečejo tudi *the man what lives next door*; pisava hoče who ali that.
rule.de:
**Ein Relativsatz** sagt, welche Person oder Sache du meinst. Er steht nach dem Nomen, ohne Komma, und **who** ändert sich nie: kein der, die, das.

**who** ist für Menschen: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** (Der Mann, der nebenan wohnt, ist Schmied.) **which** ist für Dinge: **the bus which goes to Keswick**. **that** ist für beides und sehr häufig: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down**.

Kommt gleich danach ein neues Subjekt, ist das Wort Objekt und kann wegfallen: **the cheese (that) Arthur likes** (der Käse, den Arthur mag), **the man (who) I met**. Als Subjekt bleibt es: **the man who lives next door**. Kein Pronomen kommt dazu: **the book I read**, nie *the book I read it*.

**where** ist für Orte: **the inn where we had lunch**. **whose** steht für his, her, their: **the man whose dog won** (der Mann, dessen Hund gewonnen hat). Das kleine Wort bleibt am Ende: **the woman I spoke to** (die Frau, mit der ich gesprochen habe), **the inn we had lunch at**.

Man sagt auch *the man what lives next door*; geschrieben steht who oder that.
rule.it:
**Una relativa** dice quale persona o cosa intendi. Sta dopo il nome, senza virgola.

**who** è per le persone: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** (L'uomo che abita qui accanto è un fabbro.) **which** è per le cose: **the bus which goes to Keswick**. **that** è per tutti e due ed è molto comune: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down**.

Se subito dopo viene un nuovo soggetto, la parola è oggetto e può cadere, cosa che *che* non può fare: **the cheese (that) Arthur likes** (il formaggio che piace ad Arthur), **the man (who) I met**. Come soggetto resta: **the man who lives next door**. Non si aggiunge un pronome: **the book I read**, mai *the book I read it*.

**where** è per i luoghi: **the inn where we had lunch**. **whose** sta per his, her, their: **the man whose dog won** (l'uomo il cui cane ha vinto). La parolina resta in fondo: **the woman I spoke to** (la donna con cui ho parlato), **the inn we had lunch at**.

Si dice anche *the man what lives next door*; per iscritto si usa who o that.
rule.en:
A **relative clause** says which person or thing you mean. It follows the noun, with no comma.

**who** is for people: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** **which** is for things: **the bus which goes to Keswick**. **that** is for both and is very common: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down**.

When a new subject comes straight after it, the word is the object and can go: **the cheese (that) Arthur likes**, **the man (who) I met**. As the subject it stays: **the man who lives next door**. No pronoun comes in: **the book I read**, never *the book I read it*.

**where** is for places: **the inn where we had lunch**. **whose** stands for his, her, their: **the man whose dog won**. A small word stays at the end: **the woman I spoke to**, **the inn we had lunch at**.

People also say *the man what lives next door*; writing wants who or that.

examples.sl: Mož, ki živi zraven, je kovač.

note.en: A person, the subject: who stays.

examples.en: This is the bus that goes to Keswick.
examples.sl: To je avtobus, ki pelje v Keswick.
examples.de: Das ist der Bus, der nach Keswick fährt.
examples.it: Questo è l'autobus che va a Keswick.

examples.sl: To je sir, ki ga ima Arthur rad.
examples.de: Das ist der Käse, den Arthur mag.
examples.it: Questo è il formaggio che piace ad Arthur.

note.sl: Predmet: that odpade, brez it na koncu.
note.de: Objekt: that fällt weg, kein it am Ende.
note.it: Oggetto: that cade, senza it in fondo.
note.en: The object: that can go, with no it at the end.

examples.en: This is the inn where we had lunch.
examples.sl: To je gostilna, kjer smo kosili.
examples.de: Das ist das Gasthaus, wo wir zu Mittag gegessen haben.
examples.it: Questa è la locanda dove abbiamo pranzato.

examples.en: Jack is the man whose dog won the prize.
examples.sl: Jack je mož, čigar pes je dobil nagrado.
examples.de: Jack ist der Mann, dessen Hund den Preis gewonnen hat.
examples.it: Jack è l'uomo il cui cane ha vinto il premio.

examples.en: That's the woman I spoke to.
examples.sl: To je ženska, s katero sem govoril.
examples.de: Das ist die Frau, mit der ich gesprochen habe.
examples.it: È la donna con cui ho parlato.

note.en: The small word stays at the end.

tip.sl: 💡 Brez vejice in brez *ga, jo*: **the book I read** (knjiga, ki sem jo prebral).
tip.de: 💡 Kein Komma, und **who** für der, die, das: **the man who lives next door**.
tip.it: 💡 *che* non cade mai, **that** sì: **the cheese Arthur likes**.
tip.en: 💡 No comma, and no extra pronoun: **the book I read**.
